newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 70-85 bcf in wkly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 70-85 bcf in wkly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 70-85 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 45 bcf to 120 bcf for the week ended January 3.

"In spite of the warm weather, you could get a high number because cash prices encouraged withdrawals," said one Houston-based trader, noting at some point, operators were likely to cash in on the steep backwardation in prices.
In last report, overall stocks fell by 128 bcf, at the high end of expectations, but were just 54 bcf, or 2.5 percent, below year-ago. The four week average drawdown is 96 bcf.

While producing and consuming region west inventories continued to significantly lag 1995 levels, stocks in the critical eastern region, which fell in last report by 84 bcf, were still 154 bcf, or 13 percent, above year-ago.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 138 bcf. A draw today in the expected range would finally close the overall gap to last year. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 86 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 42 bcf and western stocks by 10 bcf.
